title: How to Get Cooperation
coreMove: Convert your conclusion into a question the other person can answer in their own words, then accept their answer as the plan.

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional sales director rolling out a new commission structure to twelve reps who already hate it
exampleSpecs.audience: a regional sales director who has already lost one rep to a competitor this quarter
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the team adopts the new structure as their own or quietly sandbags the rollout for six months
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director catches herself about to announce the structure, stops, and instead asks the reps what a fair commission would reward, then writes their answer on the whiteboard

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospice nurse helping a dying woman's adult son decide whether to authorize a feeding tube
exampleSpecs.audience: a hospice nurse who has watched families fracture over end-of-life decisions
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the son lives the next decade believing he chose well for his mother or believing he was talked into something
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse names what the son already seems to want out loud as a question, then waits in silence until he answers it himself

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school orchestra conductor whose first violins are dragging the tempo every rehearsal
exampleSpecs.audience: a second-year orchestra teacher who keeps tapping the stand louder
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the section plays the spring concert with confidence or with the conductor's resentment baked into every measure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the conductor stops correcting the tempo and instead asks the section leader to count off what tempo the piece wants, accepting the slightly slow tempo she names

exampleSpecs.domain: a divorced father trying to get his fourteen-year-old to stop leaving wet towels on the bathroom floor
exampleSpecs.audience: a divorced father with weekend custody and no leverage left
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the bathroom becomes a daily skirmish or the boy starts treating the apartment as partly his own
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the father resists the urge to issue a rule and instead asks the boy what a fair towel arrangement would look like, then lives with the boy's answer even though it is not what he would have chosen

exampleSpecs.domain: a city planner running a public meeting about a proposed bike lane on a contested commercial street
exampleSpecs.audience: a city planner who has been shouted down at three previous meetings
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the lane gets built with shop-owner support or with a lawsuit attached
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the planner sets aside her prepared slides and asks the room what they would need to see in a good bike-lane proposal, writing every answer on butcher paper before she says a word about her own plan

exampleSpecs.domain: a restaurant owner whose line cook keeps overcooking the duck on Saturday nights
exampleSpecs.audience: a restaurant owner who has already fired two cooks this year
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the kitchen finds its own standard for the dish or the owner spends every Saturday at the pass
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the owner sits with the cook on a Sunday morning and asks him how he would know a duck was right, then adopts the cook's answer as the house standard
